chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu al-Maghra', from al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The testimony of the man is allowed for his wife, and of the woman for her husband, when there was someone else with her.
ai.seo_question: Can a husband and wife testify for each other in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies a specific condition in Shia jurisprudence where spousal testimony is valid only when accompanied by an additional witness, thereby mitigating the risk of bias inherent in close familial relationships. It reflects the scholarly emphasis on procedural integrity in legal proceedings, ensuring that the testimony of a spouse is not considered sufficient in isolation but gains validity through corroborative presence.
